title: Linguistic domination: a republican approach
core_idea: Develops a general theory of linguistic domination by applying the republican concept of domination to interpersonal linguistic relationships: it proposes treating linguistic domination as situations in which individuals or groups are subject to an uncontrolled capacity for interference in their linguistic uses, ideology, or acquisition by other agents, and supplies conceptual tools to identify when such domination occurs (e.g. conditions like the marked language and mere discretionary conditions), with particular attention to long-settled language groups.
tldr: Proposes a systematic, republican-based framework that combines sociolinguistic and political theory to define and diagnose linguistic domination in everyday interpersonal relations within multilingual, mixed territories, aiming to clarify when linguistic interference counts as domination.
